body.name: Exact-dyadic directed-rounding model \(\mathbb F_n^{\mathrm{dir}}\)
body.construction: The deterministic input consists of exact signed dyadic arrays \(\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C\) and exact dyadic control values, or certified dyadic control intervals, with numerator and exponent bit length at most \(L_n\). Computation uses MPFR-equivalent radix-two arithmetic with a \(q_n\)-bit normalized significand, correctly rounded operations in both round-toward-minus-infinity and round-toward-plus-infinity modes, and an arbitrary-precision signed exponent. Overflow and subnormal values therefore do not occur in this abstract model. An IEEE 754 backend must instead apply certified exact power-of-two rescaling, widen its exponent range before endpoint emission whenever an overflow or subnormal flag is possible, and reject every flushed value. Bit cost counts \(n,L_n,p_n,q_n,\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\) and the bit lengths of all dynamically stored exponents.
